guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
A past extraordinary opening can also become a reference point without becoming something you have to recreate. If an altered state once showed you a depth of love or wellbeing you had never imagined, that matters. But “I experienced it once,” “I can access it only in a particular state,” and “I can contact it reliably in ordinary life” are three different things.

The beautiful state can become a hook too. A psychedelic opening, dream, hypnosis session, meditation high, or sudden flood of love can become the new standard, and ordinary life then feels like failure. Intensity, relief, beauty, or a sense of revelation does not prove historical truth or completed healing. Look for what becomes more honest, protective, and reliable after the state ends.

If the child cannot receive the love, don’t answer by escalating the intensity or trying to force another breakthrough. Meet whatever is preventing the transfer.

after:
## Altered States Can Require Reparenting

Have you ever been attacked by a literal demon? Maybe during sleep paralysis or meditation or on a psychedelic trip? A lot of modern folk laugh at this, yet it’s really quite a common experience. I was being psychically attacked by ghosts in my home as a child. Because I was literally a child, I was an easy target. And since most people never actually grew up, they are easy targets for every kind of influence, including spirit influence.
brief:
- the main points, in the guide's order: (1) a past extraordinary opening can stay a reference point without becoming something you have to recreate; if an altered state once showed you a depth of love or wellbeing you'd never imagined, that matters; but experiencing it once, being able to reach it only in a particular state, and reaching it reliably in ordinary life are three different things. (2) The beautiful state can become a hook too: a psychedelic opening, a dream, a hypnosis session, a meditation high or a sudden flood of love can become the new standard, and then ordinary life feels like failure; however intense, relieving, beautiful or revelatory it was, that doesn't prove what you saw historically happened, or that your healing is complete; look for what becomes more honest, protective and reliable after the state ends. (3) If your little one can't receive the love, don't answer by escalating the intensity or forcing another breakthrough; meet whatever is keeping the love from getting through.
- already in the article, so said briefly or pointed back to, not said again: How Much Happiness Do You Know Is Possible? says "what if you've had a big spiritual experience, and it showed you a kind of peace, or a love, you didn't know existed? Then "I want you to be happy" means something much bigger, almost overnight", and tells you to "watch the fruits" of a spiritual path. When the Urge to Escape Arrives (earlier) says intensive meditation or psychedelics can get you past the guards before there's a grown-up big enough to hold what comes through, and lists his caution signs. A Heart-to-Child Loop says if no love comes back, keep sending yours.
- no drug amounts, doses or recipes, and no stories from the author's life (his own stories come in the next section).
